A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EEG-MoCE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-subject benchmark results, ablations, curvature analyses, computational measurements, and five-seed experiments, including additional Cognitive Word Generation results in Appendix D.3.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, robustness experiments, and supplementary Cognitive Word Generation evaluation in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The encoders, learnable modality curvatures, mean fusion curvature, curvature-guided attention, classifier, and training pipeline are retained. The corrected appendix distance statement aligns with Equation (2), already referenced by Algorithm 1 in both versions, rather than establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EAV emotion recognition, ISRUC-S3 sleep staging, and Cognitive N-back and Word Generation tasks with the same modalities and populations. Word Generation was already included in v1 Appendix D.3; its appearance in v3 Appendix B.4 is a relocation.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark, seed-robustness, runtime, and Word Generation comparisons retain the same comparator membership. This includes HEEGNet on EAV, XSleepFusion on ISRUC, and EF-Net on Cognitive. Updated citation metadata does not introduce replacement baselines.

E3.justification: Equation (35) revises the stated balanced-accuracy calculation from average one-versus-rest accuracy to average class recall. Section 4 also replaces the rule concerning fewer than 10 source domains with an explicit rule for at most 10 subjects, separating subject grouping from session adaptation. V1 already identifies ISRUC as leave-one-subject-out; reruns or changed realized splits are not established.

E4.justification: Architecture and component ablations, single-modality comparisons, t-SNE visualizations, seed robustness, and fusion-curvature analyses are retained. The single-modality and mean-versus-learnable fusion-curvature analyses move from the main text to v3 Appendices B.2–B.3 without new experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations in Table 9, fold-level uncertainty elsewhere, the same EAV significance statement, and paired equivalence testing with a margin of ±0.005 for fusion curvature. No run-count or statistical-reporting practice changes are documented.

E6.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the reported EEG hyperbolicity range from 0.097–0.183 to 0.097–0.202 and changes the description from consistently having the lowest values to generally having small values. This matches the unchanged Table 1. Benchmark scores, ablation results, seed statistics, runtime measurements, and plotted findings are otherwise retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3.2 removes the inconsistent identity d_L²(p,q) = −2/|K_f| − 2⟨p,q⟩_L and explicitly uses the geodesic distance defined in Equation (2). Equation (35) also corrects balanced accuracy to the class average of TP/(TP+FN). The remaining mathematical framework and algorithm are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: a hyperbolic framework for EEG-based multimodal learning, modality-specific learnable curvatures, curvature-guided fusion, and state-of-the-art cross-subject performance. No central scientific claim is added or removed.

C2.justification: Although the reported EEG hyperbolicity observation is corrected, the explanations connecting hierarchy, curvature, attention contribution, and multimodal complementarity remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning hierarchical modalities, computational stability and overhead, fusion design, and interpretability.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces 'Code will be released' with a concrete code-repository link, adding access information. The documented preprocessing, PyTorch implementation, RTX 4090 hardware, optimizers, learning rate, and training budget are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes include publication metadata for Hyper-MML and author/year updates for existing references, rather than additional literature or a revised relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and protocol clarifications, updates affiliations, funding, publication text, and bibliography formatting, and reorganizes the appendices. Experimental details move from D to B, dataset details move to C.2, and two existing analyses leave the main text; the overall narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is visually restyled while preserving its architecture. Existing displays are relocated and renumbered: single-modality Table 8 becomes appendix Table 10, runtime Table 10 becomes Table 8, and Table 11 moves to the appendix. Other changes mainly concern placement and page reflow.

improvement.justification: V3 improves precision by correcting the balanced-accuracy formula, resolving the appendix attention-distance inconsistency, and aligning the hyperbolicity discussion with Table 1. Clearer subject/session roles and a concrete code link improve reproducibility documentation. These are useful but limited gains: the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish recomputation under the corrected metric definition.
